## 開篇固定收益論點

8月18日美國固定收益市場收盤止住長端賣勢，但尚未扭轉趨勢。2年期美債殖利率持平於4.19%，5年期下降1個基點至4.37%，10年期下降1個基點至4.71%，30年期回落3個基點至5.28%。2s10s曲線趨平1個基點至52個基點，2s30s收窄3個基點至109個基點。這波收盤前的漲勢值得注意：10年期殖利率盤中一度升至4.75%，30年期也觸及約5.32%-5.33%，全球存續期間資產跌勢進一步擴大後，買盤才收復部分失地。不過，這不代表市場重返通膨降溫交易；30年期殖利率近1個月仍上升22個基點，10年期也仍上升16個基點。

市場內部結構比名目殖利率的小幅變動更為正面。10年期實質殖利率下降3個基點至2.41%，10年期損益兩平通膨率則上升2個基點至2.30%。美國與伊朗僵局使Brent維持在$91以上，投資人略為提高通膨補償要求；但實質折現率降幅足以帶動名目指標殖利率在收盤時走低。這只在邊際上逆轉前一交易日由實質殖利率主導的賣勢，並未改變趨勢。財政供給、對價格更敏感的主權債買方，以及人工智慧建設衍生的舉債需求，仍把長存續期間資產的必要報酬推在高檔。

最新美國數據支持尾盤企穩，但未構成決定性的成長衝擊。7月工業生產上升0.2%，低於0.3%的預期；6月增幅則由0.1%上修至0.3%，呈現當期偏弱、前期轉強。再加上先前公布的7月非農就業減少23,000人、通膨放緩，以及零售銷售創逾1年最大降幅，足以降低市場對聯準會立即升息的疑慮。選擇權部位轉向防範最終降息，交換市場則反映9月緊縮9個基點、至2027年6月累計約緊縮40個基點。殖利率曲線因此同時定價兩個時間尺度：下次會議行動的急迫性降低，長期資金成本卻依舊高昂。

風險資產反映了後一項負擔。費城半導體指數下跌4.98%，Nasdaq 100下跌1.68%，S&P 500下跌0.69%。VIX上升4.28%，但收在仍屬溫和的15.84。WTI近乎持平於$84.52，Brent上升0.58%至$91.40，美元指數也變動不大。美元與波動率均未急升，顯示市場並未發生廣泛融資事件。相反地，在AI相關借款人正從公開與私募信用市場籌集創紀錄資金之際，科技股重挫凸顯市場對折現率與融資成本的敏感度集中在特定部位。

信用初級市場仍能順利消化供給，但交易條件顯示，取得資金與取得低成本資金已是兩回事。Blackstone支持的QTS Realty為一座美國喬治亞州、與Microsoft相關的資料中心發行$39億5年期投資等級債券，定價殖利率7.228%；最高認購需求達$230億，最終殖利率較初始指引收窄40個基點。6倍認購看似強勁，但殖利率已與較低品質債券相當，評等僅Baa3與BBB-，且設有2年不可贖回期，反映投資人對施工、架構與集中度風險所要求的補償。整體信用市場仍有序，LQD上升0.13%，HYG與JNK僅下跌約0.10%-0.11%。這些基金走勢無法判定現券利差方向，卻顯示當日壓力集中在長存續期間與個別發行人風險，而非普遍性的信用資產拋售。

全球市場未能提供單一、足以抵銷壓力的存續期間錨點。德國透過聯合承銷發行EUR40億30年期公債，殖利率3.783%，為15年來最高的長期借款成本；法國財政與選舉風險則把30年期殖利率推向4.90%，10年期公債對德國利差擴大至85個基點。日本5年期公債標售需求為2025年6月以來最強，但財政不確定性與市場預期日本央行將加快政策正常化，使超長券買方保持審慎，20年期與30年期殖利率仍上升。中國走勢相反：7月經濟活動疲弱、寬鬆預期升高，使30年期殖利率降至2.15%，為11月以來最低，10s30s曲線趨平至約50個基點。全球共同主題並非同步緊縮，而是財政可信度、通膨限制、買方結構與在地成長差異，正使各地存續期間資產出現截然不同的定價。

## 實質殖利率回落阻止盤中跌勢擴大

週二收盤最適合解讀為長端賣勢未能延續，而非明確反轉。美債早盤隨全球主權債走弱，10年期殖利率升至接近4.75%的19個月高點，30年期更觸及2007年以來最高水準。8月交易清淡、企業月度發債量創紀錄，以及市場再度擔憂油價，均助長這波走勢。不過，截至紐約時間下午5時，5年期以上各附息券種全數回升，其中30年期漲幅最大。2s30s小幅趨平，顯示買方在長端殖利率升至極端水準後進場，對預期政策利率的看法則大致未變。

通膨市場顯示，這波買盤仍有前提。美國總統Donald Trump表示，美國與伊朗目前並未舉行或安排任何談判或對話，但同時稱荷姆茲海峽維持開放與運作。航運證據與價格反應均未證實情勢迅速正常化。6月備忘錄已失效，阿拉伯聯合大公國通報，伊朗朝該國發射的兩枚彈道飛彈落海；戰前全球五分之一的石油與液化天然氣均經荷姆茲海峽運輸。Brent收在$91.40，10年期損益兩平通膨率上升2個基點，顯示實體能源傳導管道仍在運作。

然而，能源並未迫使前端重新定價緊縮。WTI收盤近乎持平，2年期殖利率未動，實質殖利率則下降。近期勞動、消費與通膨數據，使交易員不再把每次油價上漲都視為聯準會即將升息。最新工業生產報告又帶來溫和的下行訊號：7月產出成長0.2%，低於預期0.1個百分點。6月增幅由0.1%上修至0.3%，因此不能據此判定趨勢疲弱；兩項讀數合併來看，仍較符合暫時觀望，而非立即緊縮。

選擇權部位更清楚凸顯兩者差異。買盤出現在押注聯準會9月按兵不動的策略，以及一旦預期利率路徑轉向降息即可受益的2027年3月與6月買權。先前利用9月與12月賣權表達利率上升情境的交易員，則在平倉部分部位。這波轉變發生在7月非農就業負成長、CPI放緩與零售需求走弱之後，反映市場為日後政策轉向避險，並不代表降息已成為基準情境。交換市場仍反映9月升息25個基點情境中的9個基點，至6月累計約緊縮40個基點；長債期貨選擇權也仍保有防範再度賣出的避險溢價。

跨資產反應說明，尾盤美債上漲不應被誤認為風險環境良性。今年以來領漲股市的半導體類股下跌近5%，Nasdaq跌幅明顯大於S&P 500。長端殖利率上升會壓低遠期盈餘的現值，但目前脆弱性也會經由資產負債表傳導。AI曝險分布於科技股、公司債、資料中心專案債、租賃支持的特殊目的公司及銀行融資，因此實質折現率重估會同時衝擊多資產投資組合的股債兩端。儘管地緣政治不確定性在較長期仍提供支撐，黃金期貨仍下跌0.71%至$4,386.50，因殖利率居高持續提高持有無息資產的機會成本。

收盤後只能得出一項範圍有限的結論。30年期美債殖利率升破5.30%後，買方願意承接；實質殖利率下降，也阻止盤中跌勢演變為另一個交易日全程的熊市陡峭化。然而，通膨補償仍上升，股票市場承受實質性的融資門檻衝擊，長債殖利率收盤仍高於5.25%。這波緩解來自估值與聯準會短期升息急迫性下降，結構性溢價並未消失。

## 財政供給決定全球清算價格

德國把全球存續期間之爭轉化為實際主權融資成本。德國財政代理機構透過聯合承銷發行EUR40億、2056年8月到期的債券，殖利率3.783%，為2011年以來德國30年期借款最高水準。訂單超過EUR380億，顯示需求相當充足；但成交殖利率仍遠高於7月規模較小的傳統30年期標售殖利率3.64%。龐大訂單證明融資管道暢通，卻不代表資金成本低廉。

未來供給輪廓說明，龐大訂單為何仍無法壓低殖利率。德國2027年預算草案顯示，淨融資需求為EUR2,040億。Commerzbank策略師Hauke Siemssen估計，明年Bund淨發行量將創EUR1,630億紀錄，高於2026年的約EUR1,370億；另有EUR2,380億債務到期，總發行量約EUR4,000億。國庫券、現金準備、資產出售，以及國營開發銀行KfW的付款，可降低Bund籌資金額，但國防與基礎建設支出仍會提高對長期儲蓄的需求。銀行聯合承銷能擴大投資人基礎並迅速籌得大筆資金，卻不會改變交易背後的財政需求。

法國則在相同全球壓力上疊加自身財政溢價。投資人為2027年預算攻防與2027年4月總統大選建立看空部位，使主力10年期公債期貨合約未平倉量升至6月初以來最高。總理Sebastien Lecornu希望在國會分裂下把赤字降至5%以下；但他警告，若無法達成協議，計畫可能延至明年，赤字最高可達6.5%。30年期殖利率升至約4.90%，為2008年以來最高；10年期公債對德國利差擴大至85個基點，為10月以來最寬。

這項利差並非全由一般利率走勢造成。Natixis策略師Theophile Legrand認為，約25個基點來自法國特有風險，為2025年12月預算緊張以來最高。財政部長Roland Lescure已將2026年成長預測由0.9%下修至0.7%，並稱要把赤字占GDP比率由2025年的5.1%降至5%相當困難。Lecornu反對加稅，火災、高溫與乾旱又帶來額外支援需求。Fitch將在8月28日展開下一輪評等決策；去年秋季，Fitch、S&P Global Ratings與Morningstar DBRS均已調降法國評等，Moody's也下修展望。政治承諾與評等日期並非同一事件，但兩者共同界定法國財政溢價高於德國的原因。

ECB首席經濟學家Philip Lane說明兩個市場面臨的貨幣政策限制。他預期歐元區通膨至年底都將維持約3%，遠高於2%目標，實際走勢則取決於伊朗衝突能否解決。7月通膨為2.9%，第二季產出成長0.4%，優於預期。Lane未承諾在6月升息25個基點後再次升息，但表示ECB必須防止通膨過高的情況延續太久，並指出明年夏季與天候有關的食品價格壓力也是額外風險。財政發債增加之際，央行容許長端殖利率下降的空間有限。

日本顯示這種組合所造成的天期偏好。5年期公債標售投標倍數為4.15倍，高於前次的3.43倍與過去12個月平均的3.34倍。標售尾差由0.03改善至0.02；結果公布後，5年期殖利率下降1.5個基點至2.145%。曲線中段殖利率處於高檔，吸引避開最脆弱區段的投資人進場。不過，買方結構仍是一項限制：76%的標售由身分未明的投標者取得，其中可能包括投資期限較短、次級市場行為不確定的持有者。

超長天期JGB未獲得相同支撐。20年期殖利率上升4個基點至3.85%，30年期上升5個基點至4.125%。首相高市早苗領導的政府尚未說明如何為食品消費稅調降2年的措施籌資；同時，日本央行正縮減購債，進口通膨與日圓疲弱也支持提高政策利率。協助管理Mizuho規模JPY41兆證券投資組合的Kenya Koshimizu表示，除抗通膨債券與1年內到期券外，該行正避開JGB。他認為9月升息機率很高，也不排除年底前升息兩次，屆時政策利率將由1%升至1.5%。這是銀行資產負債表判斷，而非日本央行指引，但也說明為何殖利率上升尚未吸引大型本土機構重新配置長存續期間部位。

因此，全球清算價格問題的成因各自不同，結果卻相同。德國面臨國防、基礎建設與到期償債需求上升；法國另有政治與評等風險；日本則同時面對財政不明朗與貨幣政策正常化。三者都能順利發債，但邊際長存續期間買方要求更高補償，使各國籌資成本都在上升。

## AI融資以風險移轉價格成交

Project Odyssey為當前AI基礎建設風險提供最清楚的定價。QTS旗下QualityTech的兩家特殊目的子公司發行$39億5年期債券，用於興建、開發及營運一座美國喬治亞州、與Microsoft相關的資料中心，也可支應一般企業用途及分配給QualityTech。交易規模比最初討論高出約$10億。最高訂單達$230億，約為發行規模6倍，也高於今年高評等債券平均約4倍的認購倍數。

最終條件顯示，不能把龐大訂單解讀為投資人不分風險追捧。殖利率在行銷期間收窄40個基點，但最終仍定在7.228%，接近較低品質信用債的水準。Moody's給予Baa3、Fitch給予BBB-評等，均為投資等級最低一級，且債券2年內不得贖回。專案執行、租戶集中與剩餘資產價值風險都落在Microsoft一般公司債之外，投資人因此要求補償。強勁需求擴大了交易規模，卻未壓低風險溢價。

次級市場表現進一步印證這一點。QTS子公司4月以5.7%發行$46億10年期高評等債券，這批債券週二殖利率約7.16%，接近單B級債券水準。前一週另一筆$22.5億的Zenith Arc資料中心債券也已走弱。價格發現正從借款人的評等標籤轉向底層經濟結構。反覆發債、施工曝險，以及對少數AI租戶的依賴，可能使名義上高評等的專案債表現得更像投機等級信用債。

Alphabet正透過另一條管道取得同一批全球儲蓄資金。其首次澳幣發債規劃4種天期，目標規模約A$50億，即$36億。3年期債券初始指引約為澳洲指標利率加80個基點；類似的美元Alphabet債券換匯為澳幣後，利差約56個基點。其他券次最初給予當地投資人的收益，也比換匯後的美元同類債券高約20-25個基點。新市場發債通常會提供部分讓利，且訂單進場後可能收窄，因此這些水準並非最終融資成本。儘管如此，Alphabet繼美元、瑞士法郎、英鎊、歐元、加幣與日圓後，仍願意支付成本以分散資金來源。

借款需求已不再只是Alphabet營運計畫的附帶項目。公司把2026年資本支出預測提高至最高$2,050億，評等分析師也警告，超大規模雲端業者的債務增速高於營收。變現能力與投入資本報酬率將決定，今日基礎建設債務能否繼續獲得充分支撐，或對AI支出轉化為盈餘速度較慢的發行人構成壓力。JPMorgan Asset Management的Gabriela Santos估計，公開與私募市場AI資本支出合計達$5.5兆，並強調固定收益曝險如今與股票曝險重疊。真正需要關注的集中度是一整套融資生態系，而非單一產業標籤。

其他私募交易顯示這套生態系的觸角有多廣。為美國軍方與商業客戶提供服務、由Boeing與Lockheed Martin合資的火箭公司United Launch Alliance，把私募債融資規模由原先$5億提高至$15億，發行4種券次，天期介於3年至10年。Ripple Prime則發行$2.75億、2031年到期的優先無擔保債券，票息8.25%，獲KBRA給予BBB評等；隨其美國主經紀業務擴張，資金將用於一般企業用途。私募可避開波動較大的公開市場執行風險，但這些交易仍鎖定高額票息，並把更多科技相關曝險移轉給機構放款人。

整體供給創紀錄，也把信用市場重新連結到美債。截至週一，8月投資等級債券發行量已超過$1,450億，當日另有12家發行人增加$91億供給。政府赤字與AI借款人的風險不可互換，但兩者競逐的是相同存續期間承接能力。週二美債回升顯示，只要殖利率夠高，需求就會重新出現；Project Odyssey也在信用市場說明同一點，只是所需利差更大，結構性保護也更明確。

## 在地曲線回報政策差異

中國長端上漲，是當日全球債市賣勢最鮮明的反例。30年期公債殖利率降至2.15%，為11月底以來最低；與10年期公債的利差收窄至約50個基點，接近2月以來最窄。30年期公債期貨未平倉量週五創下紀錄。7月產出、零售銷售與投資疲弱，提高市場對貨幣寬鬆及經濟長期疲軟的預期；即使美國、歐洲與日本殖利率上升，中國市場仍有延長存續期間的國內理由。

這波上漲有兩項限制。Shanze Fund的Song Xiaofei認為，主要動能來自短線交易型投資組合，而非持久的機構配置。曲線趨平也會壓縮銀行淨利差；相較全球市場的殖利率劣勢擴大，則可能加劇資本外流與人民幣壓力。地方政府上半年發債落後進度後，預計第三季將加速至歷史新高，可能中斷這波走勢。Song表示，10s30s利差若要維持在40個基點以下，債券供給必須放緩，長期買方也必須參與。中國存續期間資產走強，反映國內需求疲弱與金融流動性充裕，而非全球通膨風險下降。

印度顯示，央行工具可以逆轉殖利率曲線的一個區段，同時開啟另一條融資管道。印度儲備銀行吸引超過$500億後，提前1個月終止外幣存款獎勵措施，出乎原先預期窗口仍將開放的市場意料。Citigroup把預估流入金額下調$100億至$700億，Nomura則由最高$900億下調至約$720億。銀行先前把所取得的大部分盧比流動性投入4年至5年期公債，因此窗口關閉縮短熱門陡峭化交易的延續空間，也提高近期再融資壓力。

另一項工具則讓境外借款管道持續開放至12月，平均天期至少3年的交易可享1.5%固定年換匯利率。ICICI Bank週一發行$7.5億美元債券，使印度金融機構2026年發行量升至$88.5億，已高於2019年全年$79.2億的前次紀錄。Kotak Mahindra Bank正準備發行5年期債券，Yes Bank也已聘任顧問。強勁訂單使近期交易得以較初始指引收窄。可能的發展順序是近期境外發債日程加速，待特殊窗口關閉、一般避險成本重新主導後，發行速度再放緩。

印尼市場對一項執行仍不確定的財政承諾給予正面反應。總統Prabowo Subianto的2027年計畫把赤字目標定為GDP的2.4%，低於3%法定上限，且未增加另一項重大支出計畫。印尼股市週二上升0.8%，較6月低點累計上升約21%；5年期公債殖利率下降4個基點，降至6月18日以來最低。過去兩週10年期殖利率已下降16個基點，投資人對央行政策延續性的信心也有所提升。

但預算並未消除供給風險。Bank of America估計，明年整體發債規模仍可能接近$440億，其中可能包括移至表面赤字之外的支出。Prabowo力求2026年與2027年均達成6%成長，而政府過去曾上修原本保守的赤字，並把資金重新配置至免費餐食計畫。務實的匯率、通膨與借款成本框架降低了眼前的尾端風險；收入成長與支出節制能否落實，將決定債券漲勢會演變為財政重評，或僅是未再出現意外後的釋然。

南韓與烏拉圭呈現不同的政策不對稱。南韓1年期隱含政策利率為3.79%，遠高於2.75%的政策利率；此前南韓央行7月升息，但7月通膨仍低於預期，放緩至2.8%。M&G的Low Guan Yi預期只會再升息25個基點，而非曲線反映的約100個基點；其理由之一是晶片業榮景使上半年企業稅收入增加9.6%至KRW49.3兆，因此追加支出未必需要增加發債。外資7月已賣出約$12億南韓公債，10年期殖利率較6月上升22個基點，這項看法因此同時面對部位與油價風險。相較之下，烏拉圭連續第4次會議把政策利率維持在5.75%。7月通膨升至4.3%，但仍低於4.5%目標；受訪機構預期要到10月會議才會升息25個基點。決定哪些主權殖利率曲線能抵抗全球賣勢的，仍是在地通膨與財政能力，而非僅由美國存續期間資產方向決定。

## 信用市場暢通仍難消治理壓力

Sammons Financial發出一項集中的警訊：整體高評等市場融資暢通，仍可能與嚴重的治理重估同時發生。其2036年6月到期債券對指標利差約2.4個百分點，高於1週前的1.47個百分點，價格跌至發行以來最低。這批債券來自6月一筆$7.5億10年期交易，2週後又發行$5億5年期債券。最新走勢延續先前的利差擴大，市場壓力也與投資人持續檢視該保險公司和Mark Walter旗下Guggenheim企業的關係有關。

Hunterbrook Media旗下投資關係企業披露持有Sammons債券空頭部位；該媒體援引Guggenheim申報文件，指出文件仍把這家保險公司列為關係人，並警告雙方財務連結可能產生偏袒Sammons的誘因。報告發布方的經濟利益是評估內容時的限制因素，但無法抹去實際市場反應。Sammons表示，母公司Sammons Enterprises只持有Guggenheim Capital無表決權、無控制力的權益，且多年來持續減持。公司並稱母公司不持有表決權或普通股權，無權控制Guggenheim Capital、TWG Global Holdings或其關係企業，旗下主管、董事與員工也未受調查。

債權人的疑問不只涉及正式表決控制權。Guggenheim曾為該保險公司管理數百億美元資產，長期以來也把Sammons視為最大股東。檢察官與監管機關正調查Walter相關保險公司發放、並流向其商業版圖其他部門的貸款。Guggenheim一筆2031年11月到期的第一順位定期貸款，週一報價低於面額的80美分，低於7月20日左右的面額水準。Fitch給予Sammons的A-評等肯定其資本非常充足，但也指出高風險資產曝險略高。即使公司否認具有法律控制權，債券持有人仍在重新定價關係人經濟利益與資產配置可能帶來的影響。

Avison Young則呈現較具建設性的風險移轉。債權人正把債權轉換為這家加拿大不動產顧問公司的股權，使年度現金利息降低逾70%，債務降至EBITDA的3倍以下。執行長Mark Rose預期資本重整將在10月完成，並表示放款人將提供額外股本，用於招募與收購，包括拓展資料中心及辦公室改建相關業務。交易完成後，合夥人仍將持有約半數股權。債權人成為股東後，公司的當前償債能力獲得改善，但再融資本身不會創造價值；未來回收更直接取決於商用不動產循環與公司能否落實成長。

這些案例界定了其他方面仍運作正常的市場邊界。QTS訂單強勁、投資等級債券發行量創紀錄，以及整體信用基金穩定，都顯示資金仍然充足。Sammons說明，投資人仍可在投資等級範圍內迅速要求治理溢價。Avison Young則顯示，放款人願意承擔股權曝險，以恢復公司的營運彈性。市場融資管道廣泛暢通，但控制權、擔保品與未來企業價值如何分配，已與票息同等重要。

## 前瞻市場意涵

8月19日公布的7月FOMC會議紀要，以及主席Kevin Warsh下週在Jackson Hole的談話，需要說明聯準會能否在降低近期升息急迫性的同時，容忍長期通膨補償走高。收盤曲線顯示2年期殖利率持平、10年期損益兩平通膨率上升2個基點、10年期實質殖利率下降3個基點。若政策說明聚焦於就業、通膨與零售需求放緩後保持耐心，這種分化將得以延續，財政與企業供給也仍會是長端主要負擔。若對油價傳導或緊縮程度不足的憂慮升高，前端將重新與損益兩平通膨率連動，挑戰週二尾盤的實質殖利率緩解。

下一輪長存續期間供給考驗來自日本與美國基礎建設融資。日本8月20日的20年期公債標售接續強勁的5年期標售，但起點是20年期殖利率已達3.85%、超長天期JGB需求不確定，而且政府尚未為食品稅調降措施籌措財源。結果若疲弱，代表曲線中段需求無法延伸至財政與政策存續期間風險。大華府都會區機場管理局8月19日將表決是否把資本預算增加$155億，資金主要來自$142億債券；若獲通過，將對投資人承接能力形成規模異常龐大的未來市政債需求。提案涵蓋5項營建方案，成本$199億，其中$44億已獲核准；表決通過只會建立融資計畫，並非立即發債。

荷姆茲海峽仍是足以同時改變通膨與風險結論的實體條件。船舶交通確實恢復、運費與保險成本下降，以及原油走低，將減輕使Brent停留在$91.40的壓力，並可能讓實質殖利率帶動的債市漲勢擴大。若僵局持續、再有攻擊，或航運受到更有效的阻斷，能源傳導至實際通膨與央行政策的機率將上升，而不再主要停留在長端溢價。若2年期殖利率與損益兩平通膨率同步上升，核心論點將出現實質變化；若再度由長端實質殖利率上升帶動曲線陡峭化，則會證實財政供給與AI融資仍是存續期間資產的主要限制。

overall_summary.headline: 實質殖利率回落打斷長端賣勢，但尚未終結
overall_summary.session_narrative: 全球賣壓把殖利率推至新的盤中極端後，長天期美債於紐約收盤前回升，殖利率曲線小幅趨平，並未反轉趨勢。美國經濟活動數據偏弱，降低市場對聯準會下一步行動的急迫感，實質殖利率下降也蓋過通膨補償上升的影響。油價風險、主權債供給與持續擴大的AI融資需求，仍使存續期間資產價格高昂；科技股下跌則凸顯折現率偏高的跨資產成本，但未顯示廣泛融資事件。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The August 18 U.S. fixed-income close interrupted the long-end selloff without resolving it. The 2-year Treasury yield held at 4.19%, the 5-year fell 1 basis point to 4.37%, the 10-year declined 1 basis point to 4.71%, and the 30-year retraced 3 basis points to 5.28%. The 2s10s curve flattened 1 basis point to 52 and 2s30s narrowed 3 basis points to 109. That closing rally matters because the 10-year had traded as high as 4.75% and the 30-year reached roughly 5.32%-5.33% intraday, extending the global duration break before buyers recovered part of the loss. It does not mark a return to the disinflation rally: the 30-year remained 22 basis points higher over 1 month and the 10-year was still 16 basis points higher.

The internal composition was more constructive than the small nominal moves suggest. The 10-year real yield fell 3 basis points to 2.41%, whereas the 10-year breakeven rose 2 basis points to 2.30%. Investors required slightly more inflation compensation as the U.S.-Iran impasse kept Brent above $91, yet the real discount rate eased enough to pull the nominal benchmark lower by the close. This reverses the prior session's real-yield-led selloff at the margin, not in trend. Fiscal supply, a more price-sensitive sovereign buyer base and the debt demands of the artificial-intelligence buildout continue to set a high long-duration hurdle.

Fresh U.S. evidence supported the late stabilization but did not deliver a decisive growth shock. July industrial production rose 0.2%, below the 0.3% expectation, while June was revised up to 0.3% from 0.1%. The softer current reading followed stronger history. Alongside the previously reported decline of 23,000 in July payrolls, softer inflation and the largest retail-sales drop in more than a year, it was enough to reduce concern about an immediate Federal Reserve increase. Options activity shifted toward protection against eventual cuts, and swaps embedded 9 basis points of tightening for September and about 40 basis points by June 2027. The curve is consequently pricing two horizons at once: less urgency at the next meeting and a persistently expensive long-run cost of capital.

Risk assets revealed the burden of that second horizon. The semiconductor index fell 4.98%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 1.68%, and the S&P 500 declined 0.69%. The VIX rose 4.28% but ended at a restrained 15.84. WTI was nearly unchanged at $84.52, Brent added 0.58% to $91.40, and the Dollar Index was also little changed. The absence of a dollar or volatility surge argues against a broad funding event. Instead, the sharp technology decline exposed a concentrated sensitivity to discount rates and financing costs just as AI-related borrowers are drawing record amounts from public and private credit markets.

Primary credit still cleared, though the terms show that access and cheap capital have separated. Blackstone-backed QTS Realty priced $3.9 billion of five-year investment-grade notes for a Microsoft-linked Georgia data center at 7.228%, after attracting as much as $23 billion of peak demand and tightening the yield by 40 basis points. The six-times book looks strong; a yield comparable with lower-quality debt, ratings at Baa3 and BBB-, and a two-year non-call period show what investors required for construction, structure and concentration risk. Broad credit remained orderly, with LQD up 0.13% and HYG and JNK down only about 0.10%-0.11%. Those fund moves do not identify cash-spread direction, but they place the day's stress in long-duration and issuer-specific risk rather than generalized credit liquidation.

Global markets supplied no single offsetting duration anchor. Germany paid 3.783% on a EUR4 billion 30-year syndication, its highest long borrowing cost in 15 years, while French fiscal and election risk pushed the 30-year yield toward 4.90% and the 10-year spread over Germany to 85 basis points. Japan's five-year auction drew its strongest demand since June 2025, but 20- and 30-year yields rose as fiscal uncertainty and expectations of faster Bank of Japan normalization kept superlong buyers cautious. China moved in the opposite direction: its 30-year yield fell to 2.15%, the lowest since November, as weak July activity and easing expectations flattened the 10s30s curve toward 50 basis points. The common global story is not synchronized tightening. It is that fiscal credibility, inflation constraints, buyer composition and local growth are producing sharply different prices for duration.

## Real-Yield Relief Stops an Intraday Break

Tuesday's close is best understood as a failed extension of the long-end selloff rather than a clean reversal. Treasuries weakened with global sovereign bonds early in the session, taking the 10-year yield to a 19-month high near 4.75% and the 30-year to its highest level since 2007. Thin August conditions, record monthly corporate supply and renewed concern over oil all reinforced the move. By 5:00 p.m. New York, however, every coupon maturity from 5 years onward had recovered, with the largest rally in the 30-year. The small flattening in 2s30s shows buyers responding to an extreme long-end level while leaving the expected policy rate broadly unchanged.

The inflation market kept that response conditional. President Donald Trump said no talks or conversations with Iran were taking place or scheduled, even as he described the Strait of Hormuz as open and operating. Shipping evidence and the price response did not validate a rapid normalization. The June memorandum had expired, the United Arab Emirates reported that two Iranian ballistic missiles fell into the sea after being fired toward the country, and a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas had transited Hormuz before the war. Brent's $91.40 close and the 2-basis-point rise in the 10-year breakeven show that the physical energy channel remained live.

Yet energy did not force a renewed front-end tightening move. WTI finished almost unchanged, the 2-year yield did not move, and real yields fell. Recent labor, consumer and inflation readings have made traders less willing to treat every oil rise as an imminent Fed increase. The latest industrial-production report added a modest downside signal: July output grew 0.2%, one-tenth below expectations. June's revision from 0.1% to 0.3% prevents a weak-trend conclusion, but the combination was compatible with waiting rather than tightening immediately.

Options positioning sharpened that distinction. Buyers appeared in September structures aimed at a Fed hold and in March and June 2027 calls that benefit if the expected path shifts toward cuts. Traders who had used September and December puts to express higher-rate outcomes were liquidating some of those positions. The change followed the negative July payroll reading, softer CPI and weaker retail demand. It is a hedge against a later policy pivot, not evidence that cuts have become the central outcome. Swaps still priced 9 basis points of a quarter-point rise for September and around 40 basis points of tightening by June, and options on long-bond futures retained a premium for protection against another selloff.

The cross-asset response explains why the late Treasury rally should not be mistaken for a benign risk session. Semiconductor shares suffered a nearly 5% decline after leading this year's equity performance, and the Nasdaq fell substantially more than the S&P 500. Higher long yields reduce the present value of distant earnings, but the vulnerability now also runs through balance sheets. AI exposure sits in technology equity, corporate bonds, data-center project debt, lease-backed special-purpose vehicles and bank facilities. A repricing of the real discount rate therefore reaches both sides of a multi-asset portfolio. Gold futures fell 0.71% to $4,386.50 as elevated yields continued to raise the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset, even though geopolitical uncertainty remained supportive over a longer horizon.

The completed close leaves a narrow conclusion. Buyers were willing to absorb 30-year Treasuries at yields above 5.30%, and the real-yield decline prevented an intraday break from becoming another full-session bear steepening. Inflation compensation still rose, equities registered a material financing-hurdle shock, and the long bond ended above 5.25%. Relief came from valuation and a less urgent Fed path; the structural premium was not removed.

## Fiscal Supply Sets Global Clearing Prices

Germany converted the global duration debate into a realized sovereign financing cost. The finance agency sold EUR4 billion of debt maturing in August 2056 through a syndicate at 3.783%, the highest yield for German 30-year borrowing since 2011. Orders exceeded EUR38 billion, so the sale demonstrated substantial demand. Its clearing level still stood well above the 3.64% yield on a smaller conventional 30-year auction in July. The book established access, not a low cost of capital.

The forward supply profile explains why a large book did not cap yields. Germany's 2027 draft budget points to a EUR204 billion net financing requirement. Commerzbank strategist Hauke Siemssen estimates record net Bund issuance of EUR163 billion next year, up from about EUR137 billion in 2026, with gross sales around EUR400 billion as EUR238 billion of debt matures. Bills, cash reserves, asset sales and payments from state development bank KfW can reduce the amount raised in Bunds, but defense and infrastructure spending still increase the long-run claim on savings. A bank syndication broadens the investor base and raises a large amount quickly; it does not change the fiscal requirement behind the transaction.

France added an idiosyncratic fiscal premium to the same global pressure. Open interest in the active 10-year futures contract rose to its highest since early June as investors established bearish positions ahead of the 2027 budget fight and the April 2027 presidential election. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is seeking a deficit below 5% in a divided parliament, but has warned that failure to agree could delay a plan into next year and leave the deficit as high as 6.5%. The 30-year yield reached about 4.90%, the highest since 2008, and the 10-year spread to Germany widened to 85 basis points, its broadest since October.

Not all of that spread is a generic rates move. Natixis strategist Theophile Legrand attributes about 25 basis points to France-specific risk, the most since budget tensions in December 2025. Finance Minister Roland Lescure has already reduced the 2026 growth forecast to 0.7% from 0.9% and described the goal of cutting the deficit to 5% of GDP from 5.1% in 2025 as difficult. Lecornu has resisted tax increases, while fires, heat and drought are creating additional demands for support. Fitch begins the next sequence of rating decisions on August 28 after Fitch, S&P Global Ratings and Morningstar DBRS downgraded France in the prior autumn and Moody's lowered its outlook. Political promises and rating dates are not the same event, but together they define why France trades with a larger fiscal premium than Germany.

ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane supplied the monetary constraint facing both markets. He expects euro-area inflation to remain around 3% through year-end, well above the 2% target, depending on whether the Iran conflict is resolved. July inflation was 2.9%, and second-quarter output expanded 0.4%, stronger than expected. Lane did not commit to another increase after June's quarter-point move, but said the ECB must prevent inflation from staying too high for too long and identified weather-related food pressure as an additional risk next summer. Fiscal issuance is rising into a policy environment where the central bank has limited room to validate lower long yields.

Japan demonstrated the maturity preference created by that mix. The five-year government auction posted a 4.15 bid-to-cover ratio, up from 3.43 at the previous sale and above the 3.34 12-month average. Its 0.02 tail improved from 0.03, and the five-year yield fell 1.5 basis points to 2.145% after the result. Elevated belly yields attracted demand as investors avoided the most exposed part of the curve. The qualification is ownership: 76% of the sale went to unidentified bidders, potentially including shorter-horizon holders whose secondary behavior is uncertain.

Superlong JGBs received no equivalent support. The 20-year yield rose 4 basis points to 3.85% and the 30-year gained 5 basis points to 4.125%. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government has not explained how it will finance a two-year reduction in the food sales tax, and the BOJ is reducing bond purchases as imported inflation and yen weakness argue for higher policy rates. Kenya Koshimizu, who helps manage Mizuho's JPY41 trillion securities portfolio, said the bank is avoiding JGBs other than inflation-linked securities and maturities within one year. He sees a high likelihood of a September increase and would not rule out two moves by year-end, which would take the policy rate from 1% to 1.5%. That is a bank balance-sheet judgment rather than BOJ guidance, but it shows why higher yields have not yet drawn large domestic institutions back into duration.

The global clearing-price problem is consequently specific in cause and common in effect. Germany has rising defense, infrastructure and redemption needs; France adds political and rating risk; Japan combines fiscal ambiguity with monetary normalization. All three can place debt. Each is paying more because the marginal long-duration buyer requires greater compensation.

## AI Funding Clears at a Risk-Transfer Price

Project Odyssey supplied the clearest current price for AI infrastructure risk. Two special-purpose subsidiaries of QTS unit QualityTech issued $3.9 billion of five-year notes to fund construction, development and operation of a Microsoft-linked Georgia data center, along with general corporate expenses and distributions to QualityTech. The transaction was roughly $1 billion larger than initially discussed. Peak orders reached as much as $23 billion, about six times the deal size and above the roughly four-times average subscription for high-grade bonds this year.

Final terms prevent the book from being read as indiscriminate enthusiasm. The yield tightened 40 basis points during marketing but still landed at 7.228%, close to levels associated with lower-quality credit. Moody's rated the notes Baa3 and Fitch BBB-, the last investment-grade notches, and the bonds cannot be called for two years. Investors were compensated for a structure in which project execution, lease concentration and residual asset value sit outside Microsoft's ordinary corporate debt. Strong demand enlarged the deal; it did not collapse the risk premium.

Secondary performance reinforces that message. QTS subsidiaries issued $4.6 billion of 10-year high-grade debt in April at 5.7%. Those bonds traded around a 7.16% yield on Tuesday, close to single-B market levels. A separate $2.25 billion Zenith Arc data-center sale from the prior week had also weakened. The movement shows price discovery migrating from a borrower's rating label toward the economic structure underneath it. Repeated issuance, construction exposure and dependence on a small set of AI tenants can make nominally high-grade project debt behave more like speculative credit.

Alphabet is using a different route to the same global savings pool. Its debut Australian-dollar transaction was marketed in four maturities with a target near A$5 billion, or $3.6 billion. Initial guidance on the three-year notes was around 80 basis points over the Australian benchmark, compared with about 56 basis points on similar U.S.-dollar Alphabet debt after swapping it into Australian dollars. Other tranches initially offered local investors roughly 20-25 basis points more than swapped U.S. equivalents. Some concession is customary for a new market and can compress as orders arrive, so those levels are not a completed financing cost. They nonetheless show a highly rated hyperscaler paying to diversify funding after issuing in U.S. dollars, Swiss francs, sterling, euros, Canadian dollars and yen.

The borrowing requirement is no longer incidental to Alphabet's operating plan. The company raised its 2026 capital-spending forecast to as much as $205 billion, and rating analysts have warned that hyperscaler debt is growing faster than revenue. Monetization and return on invested capital will determine whether today's infrastructure debt remains comfortably supported or places pressure on issuers that convert AI spending into earnings more slowly. Gabriela Santos of JPMorgan Asset Management estimated AI capital expenditure across public and private markets at $5.5 trillion and emphasized that fixed-income exposure now overlaps with equity exposure. The relevant concentration is a financing ecosystem, not one sector label.

Other private transactions show how broadly that ecosystem is reaching. United Launch Alliance, the Boeing-Lockheed Martin rocket venture serving U.S. military and commercial customers, increased a private-bond financing to $1.5 billion from an original $500 million. It offered four tranches spanning 3 to 10 years. Ripple Prime raised $275 million of senior unsecured notes due in 2031 with an 8.25% coupon and a BBB rating from KBRA, using proceeds for general corporate purposes as its U.S. prime-brokerage business expands. Private placements can bypass volatile public execution, but these transactions still lock in substantial coupons and transfer more technology-linked exposure to institutional lenders.

Record aggregate supply is the bridge back to Treasuries. August investment-grade issuance had already exceeded $145 billion by Monday, and 12 issuers added $9.1 billion that day. Government deficits and AI borrowers are not interchangeable risks, yet they compete for the same duration capacity. Tuesday's Treasury recovery proves that demand reappears at sufficiently high yields. Project Odyssey proves the same point in credit, with a much larger spread and more explicit structural protection required.

## Local Curves Reward Policy Specificity

China's long-end rally was the day's strongest counterpoint to the global bond rout. The 30-year government yield fell to 2.15%, its lowest since late November, and the spread over 10-year notes compressed to around 50 basis points, near the narrowest since February. Open interest in 30-year bond futures reached a record on Friday. Weak July output, retail sales and investment have strengthened expectations of monetary easing and prolonged economic softness, creating a domestic reason to extend duration even as U.S., European and Japanese yields rise.

The rally carries two limitations. Song Xiaofei of Shanze Fund attributed the move primarily to short-term trading portfolios rather than durable institutional allocation. A flatter curve also compresses bank net interest margins, and a wider yield disadvantage against global markets can intensify capital-outflow and yuan pressure. Local-government issuance is expected to accelerate to a third-quarter record after lagging in the first half, which could interrupt the move. For the 10s30s spread to hold below 40 basis points, Song said debt supply would need to slow and long-horizon buyers would need to participate. China's duration strength reflects weak domestic demand and abundant financial liquidity, not a global fall in inflation risk.

India shows how a central-bank facility can reverse one segment of a curve while opening another funding channel. The Reserve Bank of India ended its foreign-currency deposit incentive a month early after attracting more than $50 billion, surprising a market that had expected the window to remain available. Citigroup reduced its estimated inflows by $10 billion to $70 billion, and Nomura cut its estimate to about $72 billion from as much as $90 billion. Because banks had deployed much of the resulting rupee liquidity into 4- to 5-year government bonds, the closure reduced the runway for a popular steepener and increased near-term refinancing pressure.

Offshore borrowing remains open through December under a separate facility offering a fixed 1.5% annual swap rate for an average maturity of at least 3 years. ICICI Bank's $750 million U.S.-dollar sale on Monday lifted 2026 issuance by Indian financial institutions to $8.85 billion, already above the prior full-year record of $7.92 billion in 2019. Kotak Mahindra Bank was preparing a five-year issue and Yes Bank had hired advisers. Strong books have allowed recent transactions to tighten from initial guidance. The likely sequence is an accelerated near-term offshore calendar followed by slower issuance when the special window closes and ordinary hedging costs again dominate.

Indonesia received a favorable current market response to a fiscal promise whose execution remains uncertain. President Prabowo Subianto's 2027 plan targets a deficit of 2.4% of GDP, below the 3% legal ceiling, without adding another major spending program. Indonesian equities rose 0.8% on Tuesday, extending their gain from June lows to about 21%, and the five-year government yield fell 4 basis points to its lowest since June 18. The 10-year yield had declined 16 basis points over the preceding two weeks as investors also gained confidence in continuity at the central bank.

The budget does not eliminate supply risk. Bank of America estimates overall debt issuance may still reach nearly $44 billion next year, potentially including spending moved below the headline deficit. Prabowo is seeking 6% growth in 2026 and 2027, and the administration has previously revised a conservative deficit higher while reallocating money toward its free-meals program. A realistic currency, inflation and borrowing-cost framework reduced the immediate tail risk. Delivery of revenue growth and spending restraint will decide whether the bond rally becomes a fiscal re-rating rather than relief at the absence of another surprise.

South Korea and Uruguay illustrate different policy asymmetries. Korea's one-year implied policy rate of 3.79% stood far above the 2.75% policy rate after the BOK's July increase, even though July inflation slowed more than expected to 2.8%. M&G's Low Guan Yi expects only another 25 basis points rather than the roughly 100 basis points embedded in the curve, citing a 9.6% rise in first-half corporate tax revenue to KRW49.3 trillion from the chip boom as a reason supplementary spending need not increase bond supply. Foreign investors had sold about $1.2 billion of Korean government bonds in July and the 10-year yield was 22 basis points higher since June, so the view confronts both positioning and oil risk. Uruguay, by contrast, held its policy rate at 5.75% for a fourth meeting. July inflation rose to 4.3% but remained below the 4.5% target, and surveyed institutions expect a quarter-point increase only at the October meeting. Local inflation and fiscal capacity, rather than the direction of U.S. duration alone, continue to determine which sovereign curves can resist the global selloff.

## Governance Stress Survives Open Credit

Sammons Financial supplied a concentrated warning that aggregate high-grade access can coexist with severe governance repricing. Its June 2036 bonds traded at a yield spread of about 2.4 percentage points over the benchmark, up from 1.47 percentage points a week earlier and their weakest level since issuance. The bonds came from a $750 million 10-year transaction in June, followed two weeks later by $500 million of five-year debt. The latest move deepened the prior widening and connected it to continued scrutiny of the insurer's relationship with Mark Walter's Guggenheim businesses.

Hunterbrook Media, whose investment affiliate disclosed a short position in Sammons bonds, cited Guggenheim filings that continued to describe the insurer as a related party and warned that financial links could create incentives to favor Sammons. That economic interest qualifies the report but does not remove the underlying market reaction. Sammons said parent Sammons Enterprises holds only a non-voting, non-controlling interest in Guggenheim Capital that it has been reducing for several years. It added that the parent has no voting or common equity and no ability to control Guggenheim Capital, TWG Global Holdings or their affiliates, and that its officers, directors and employees are not under investigation.

The creditor question extends beyond formal voting control. Guggenheim had managed tens of billions of dollars for the insurer and had long regarded Sammons as its largest shareholder. Prosecutors and regulators are examining loans made by Walter-linked insurers and directed toward other parts of his business empire. Guggenheim's first-lien term loan due November 2031 was quoted below 80 cents on the dollar on Monday, down from around par on July 20. Fitch's A- rating for Sammons cited very strong capital but also modestly elevated exposure to riskier assets. Bondholders are repricing the possibility that related-party economics and asset allocation matter even where legal control is denied.

Avison Young presents a more constructive transfer of risk. Creditors are swapping debt for equity in the Canadian real-estate advisory firm, reducing annual cash interest by more than 70% and taking debt below three times EBITDA. Chief Executive Mark Rose expects the recapitalization to close in October and said lenders will provide additional equity for hiring and acquisitions, including expansion around data centers and office conversions. Roughly half the company will remain owned by partners after closing. The transaction improves current debt service by making creditors owners; it does not create value from refinancing alone. Recovery now depends more directly on the commercial-property cycle and the firm's growth execution.

These cases define the boundary around an otherwise functional market. Strong QTS orders, record investment-grade issuance and stable broad credit funds show that cash remains available. Sammons shows that investors can still impose an abrupt governance premium inside investment grade. Avison Young shows lenders accepting equity exposure to restore operating flexibility. Access is broad, but the allocation of control, collateral and future enterprise value has become as important as the coupon.

## Forward Market Significance

The July FOMC minutes on August 19 and Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks next week need to clarify whether a less urgent near-term path can coexist with the Fed's tolerance for higher long-run inflation compensation. The completed curve has the 2-year unchanged, the 10-year breakeven 2 basis points higher and the 10-year real yield 3 basis points lower. A policy account centered on patience after softer jobs, inflation and retail demand would preserve that separation and leave fiscal and corporate supply as the main long-end burden. Greater concern about oil pass-through or insufficient restraint would reconnect the front end with breakevens and challenge Tuesday's late real-yield relief.

The next long-duration supply tests arrive through Japan and U.S. infrastructure finance. Japan's 20-year auction on August 20 follows a strong five-year sale but begins with the 20-year yield at 3.85%, superlong JGB demand uncertain and the government yet to fund its food-tax reduction. A weak result would show that belly demand does not extend to fiscal and policy-duration risk. The Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority's August 19 vote on adding $15.5 billion to its capital budget, funded mainly by $14.2 billion of bonds, would establish an unusually large future municipal claim on investor capacity if approved. The proposal covers five construction packages costing $19.9 billion, of which $4.4 billion is already authorized; approval would create a funding program, not an immediate bond sale.

Hormuz remains the physical condition capable of changing both the inflation and risk conclusions. Actual restoration of vessel traffic, lower freight and insurance costs, and declining crude would reduce the pressure that left Brent at $91.40 and could allow the real-yield rally to broaden. Continued deadlock, further attacks or more effective disruption would raise the probability that energy feeds into realized inflation and central-bank policy rather than remaining mostly a long-end premium. The thesis changes materially if the 2-year yield and breakevens begin rising together; another steepening led by real long rates would instead confirm that fiscal supply and AI financing remain the dominant constraints on duration.

India, Indonesia, Korea and Uruguay likewise showed that funding facilities, fiscal delivery and local policy paths can outweigh the direction of U.S. duration.

section_summaries.market_read: Broad market access does not prevent abrupt repricing when governance or control is uncertain.
section_summaries.next_check: Sammons asset links and Avison Young's October closing will test each risk transfer.
section_summaries.summary: Sammons bonds repriced sharply as investors examined related-party economics despite denied legal control, while Avison Young shifted risk to creditors through a debt-for-equity recapitalization. Functional aggregate credit markets therefore coexist with issuer-level premiums for governance, collateral and control.

section_summaries.market_read: The rally broadens only if policy patience, supply absorption and physical energy relief align.
section_summaries.next_check: The August 19 FOMC minutes are the nearest test of patience versus oil-pass-through concern.
section_summaries.summary: Three tests can distinguish temporary relief from a durable shift: Fed communication must separate patience from inflation tolerance, Japan and U.S. infrastructure decisions will probe duration capacity, and Hormuz conditions will determine whether energy pressure reaches realized inflation and policy.

overall_summary.headline: Real-yield relief interrupts the long-end selloff, without ending it
overall_summary.session_narrative: Long-end Treasuries recovered by the NY close after global selling pushed yields to fresh intraday extremes, producing a modest flattening rather than a trend reversal. Softer U.S. activity evidence reduced urgency around the next Fed move, and lower real yields outweighed higher inflation compensation. Oil risk, sovereign supply and expanding AI financing needs still kept duration expensive, while technology losses exposed the cross-asset cost of elevated discount rates without signaling a broad funding event.
